name: SN74CB3Q3384APWR
title: SN74CB3Q3384A 10-bit FET bus switch, 2.5 V / 3.3 V, high bandwidth
summary: Ten FET pass switches in two groups of five, each group with its own active-low enable (1OE, 2OE). A charge pump drives the pass-transistor gates above the supply, so the ON resistance is low (3 Ω typical) and nearly flat across the signal range, and the switches pass 0 V to 5 V with a 3.3 V supply. Data pins tolerate 5 V whether the part is powered or not, partial power-down is covered by an Ioff limit, and VCC runs from 2.3 V to 3.6 V. Offered in 24-pin SSOP/QSOP (DBQ), TSSOP (PW) and TVSOP (DGV).
key_figures: 3 Ω typ, 6 Ω max (VCC = 3 V, VI = 0, IO = 30 mA)

circuits.description: Two 50 Ω generators, each terminated by 50 Ω to ground at the part, drive the control input (VIN) and the data input (VI) of the switch under test. The data output (VO) carries CL and a 500 Ω RL to ground, plus a second RL out to switch S1. S1 is left open for propagation delay, goes to 2 × VCC for tPLZ and tPZL, and to GND for tPHZ and tPZH.

operation.text: The ten channels form two independent 5-bit switches. With nOE low a group is on and each A pin is joined to its B pin, with data free to flow either way; with nOE high the group is off and the A and B pins of that group are isolated at high impedance. The two groups serve either as two 5-bit switches or together as one 10-bit switch.

An internal charge pump lifts the gate voltage of each pass transistor. The result is a low ON resistance that changes little over the operating range, which keeps propagation delay small and lets the switch pass signals rail to rail: 0 V to 5 V with VCC = 3.3 V, and 0 V to 3.3 V with VCC = 2.5 V.
Each switch is one FET between its A and B pins. A buffer supplied by the charge pump drives the FET gate, under an internal enable signal (EN) derived from the group's OE input.

The data pins handle 0 V to 5 V signalling, including 0.8 V, 1.2 V, 1.5 V, 1.8 V, 2.5 V, 3.3 V and 5 V levels, and tolerate 5 V with the part powered or unpowered. The control inputs accept TTL levels or 5 V and 3.3 V CMOS outputs. Data and control inputs both carry undershoot clamp diodes.
Ioff is specified. With VCC at 0 V the Ioff circuitry blocks damaging current from flowing back through the part, and the ports remain isolated while it is unpowered.
For the switches to stay at high impedance while VCC ramps up or down, OE is pulled up to VCC by a resistor. How small that resistor may be is set by the current the OE driver can sink.
A control input that is not used is held at VCC or at GND for the part to work properly.

The data path reaches up to 500 MHz. I/O capacitance is low, so the switch adds little load and distortion to a bus. The control inputs may be toggled at up to 20 MHz (VCC = 3.3 V) or 10 MHz (VCC = 2.5 V); supply current rises with that rate, by 0.27 mA/MHz typical per control input.

Control and data edges are timed at VCC/2. Propagation delay is taken between VCC/2 on the input and VCC/2 on the output. Enable times end when the output crosses VCC/2; disable times end when the output has moved VΔ from its settled level, rising to VOL + VΔ (S1 at 2 × VCC, output held low inside) or falling to VOH - VΔ (S1 at GND, output held high inside).
Latch-up is above 100 mA per JESD 78, Class II. ESD is tested per JESD 22: 2000 V human-body model (A114-B, Class II) and 1000 V charged-device model (C101).

Digital and analog uses: PCI interfaces, differential signal interfaces, memory interleaving, bus isolation and low-distortion signal gating, aimed at broadband communications, networks and computing that moves much data.

PW0024A (TSSOP) and DGV0024A (TVSOP) follow JEDEC MO-153; both are 1.2 mm high at most. Their body length excludes mold flash, protrusions and gate burrs of up to 0.15 mm per side, and body width excludes interlead flash of up to 0.25 mm per side. DBQ (R-PDSO-G24) is dimensioned in inches with millimetres alongside, falls within JEDEC MO-137 variation AE, and its body dimensions exclude mold flash or protrusion of up to 0.006 in (0.15 mm) per side.

Non-solder-mask-defined pads are preferred, with the mask opening 0.05 mm larger than the pad all round; for solder-mask-defined pads the mask overlaps the metal by at least 0.05 mm. The paste stencil is 0.125 mm thick with apertures the size of the pads; trapezoidal walls and rounded corners on laser-cut apertures can improve paste release.
